claims.text: Combining GPT-3 with expert-drafted codebooks achieved substantial agreement with expert coding on question complexity (Cohen's kappa = 0.61).
Combining GPT-3 with expert-drafted codebooks achieved fair agreement with expert coding on syntactic structure (Cohen's kappa = 0.38).
Codebook-centered prompt design achieved higher agreement with experts than example-centered prompt design in deductive coding.
Shifting from a zero-shot to a one-shot prompt setting yielded the largest performance gain in agreement with human expert coders.
Performance in expert agreement did not differ substantially between one-shot and few-shot (five-shot) prompt settings.

evidence.description: Our proposed approach achieved fair to substantial agreements with expert-coded results (Question complexity: Cohen's kappa = 0.61).
Our proposed approach achieved fair to substantial agreements with expert-coded results (Syntactic Structure: Cohen's kappa = 0.38).
We found the codebook-centered design performs better than the example-centered designs, see Fig. 1.
We observed the largest performance gain when shifting from a zero-shot to a one-shot setting.
However, the performance between one-shot and few-shot settings did not differ much.

methodologies.name: GPT-3 In-Context Prompting for Deductive Coding
methodologies.description: Combining expert-drafted codebooks with GPT-3 using zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot prompting across codebook-centered and example-centered prompt designs to label qualitative data.

limitations.text: Unsupervised models are difficult to steer for complex or nuanced research questions.
Supervised models require high-quality large datasets or computing resources to achieve reasonable performance.
There remains a performance gap between human expert-to-expert agreement and LLM-to-expert agreement, with the model producing incorrect labels.
The evaluation was limited to a single case study of curiosity-driven questions and did not test generalization across varied domain contexts or nuanced coding schemes.

future_work.text: Conduct detailed error analyses on disagreed items and test LLM capability across different contexts and nuanced coding schemes.
Design interface controls and explainable AI mechanisms to calibrate user trust and prevent over-reliance on imperfect model outputs.
Investigate how to structure and write codebooks specifically optimized for LLM task performance and model comprehension.
Develop interaction techniques and Human-AI collaboration workflows to support inductive, bottom-up qualitative analysis using LLMs.
